raw_user_query: Explain about the simple electric circuit?

orchestrator_output.reformulated_query: Components and working of a simple electric circuit
orchestrator_output.text_narration: An electric circuit is a complete path through which electricity flows to make devices like a bulb glow. Today, we will learn about the main parts of a simple electric circuit and how electricity moves through it. A simple electric circuit needs four main parts to work properly. First, an electric cell provides electrical energy. Second, connecting metal wires carry the electricity. Third, a switch turns the current on or off. Fourth, an electric bulb acts as the output device that glows when current flows. Electricity can flow only when there is a continuous unbroken path. In a closed circuit, the switch is ON and the path is complete, so the bulb glows. In an open circuit, the switch is OFF or a wire is broken, creating a gap that stops the flow of current. Electric current always flows from the positive terminal of the cell, through the wire and bulb, to the negative terminal. Remember, if the bulb filament is broken, the path breaks and the bulb will not glow even in a closed switch position.
